submitted_verdict.evidence_A: Panel 1: the two selected folders sit in a bordered overlay with a letter-spaced "TRASH COLLECTOR" title, a right-aligned tally "2 items · 1.9 GiB", column captions "SELECTED ITEMS" / "ON DISK", and each row pairing a bold name with a muted "folder · path" subline and a green right-aligned size; the focused row (Browser) gets a left accent bar plus a lighter row fill, and a ruled detail block below repeats its path and "1.0 GiB allocated when scanned · 2 files". The base map, "LARGEST FIRST" list and footer are uniformly dimmed behind it. Panel 2: a second, smaller dialog stacks on top while the collector is dimmed a further step, giving three legible depth levels; the green question title, bold "1.9 GiB allocated when scanned", a boxed "Type trash to confirm:" field with cursor, and "Esc cancel" left / green "Enter move to Trash" right read as a clear hierarchy. Weaknesses: the hero numeral "1.1" is nearly invisible dark gray on black; footer key hints and "3 files · 3 folders · 2 here" are low-contrast gray; the dimmed collector shows a different detail path ("/home/diggle/W…") in panel 2 than in panel 1; the overlay hides most of the map it summarises.
submitted_verdict.evidence_B: Panel 1: selection is shown only by a filled square checkbox and a slightly brighter blue label on "Caches" and "Documents" versus empty boxes and muted lavender for the rest, plus a small "Select (2)" tab in the pane's bottom border; focus is a thin ">" chevron. The main list has seven rows in a pane roughly 600px tall, leaving most of the column empty, while the right preview column (Browser, Package cache, Thumbnails) floats unbordered against the top edge. All text is the same weight and near-identical lavender/blue, so sidebar, list, metadata and footer panes have little hierarchy. Panel 2: the confirm dialog is placed dead-centre with no dimming or tint of the background; the main pane's vertical border lines run straight into the dialog's top and bottom edges, and its border colour matches the panes, so it reads as another pane rather than a foreground layer. The warning "Are you sure you want to completely delete" (no object, no count) and the loss sentence are plain gray body text with no emphasis, while the two filled buttons give the destructive "(enter) Confirm" a calm cyan and "(q) Cancel" an alarm salmon, inverting the expected weight.
submitted_verdict.loser_reason: B's confirmation state has no foreground/background separation: the dialog uses the same lavender border and undimmed backdrop as every pane, pane borders pierce its edges, its warning text carries no emphasis, and its button colours put the alarm colour on Cancel, so the one moment that most needs a composed, readable hierarchy is the flattest screen in the entry.

submitted_verdict.evidence_A: Dense multi-panel monitor on black. Color carries meaning: per-core temperatures in blue, CPU percentages in green, memory bars coded red/yellow/blue/green per row, disk usage bars filled red, process names in cyan with root-owned rows dimmed to grey. Hierarchy is real: box titles sit on the border with red hotkey letters, column headers bolded, values right-aligned with dotted leaders. Weaknesses are visible: the red mnemonic letters inside titles ('preset', 'pause', 'reverse') read as noise; the disks panel repeats identical 69% / 190 GiB rows for root, log and home; the CPU graph region is mostly empty; the net panel's magenta/blue dot histogram has no axis labels beyond '60K'; the process list shows a '0/532' footer but no visibly highlighted selected row.
submitted_verdict.evidence_B: A treemap of six white-bordered rectangles (Caches, Games, Downloads, Projects, Photos, plus a blank one) on black. Everything is a single white weight: box borders, titles, header 'ssd-story 4.2 GiB', status line '> Caches 1.8 GiB', and the key hint row. No color is used anywhere. Boxes contain only a label; sizes are not printed inside them, so the only quantitative cue is area, which cannot be read precisely. The selected item is indicated only by a '>' in a text line under the map, not by any highlight on the Caches box itself. Interior space is empty, and the bottom-left box has no label at all.
submitted_verdict.loser_reason: B has no visual system for dense data: uniform white on black with no color, no in-box values, and a selection state that is not rendered on the map, so nothing distinguishes what matters from what doesn't.

submitted_verdict.evidence_A: Pure black ground with roughly a dozen hues applied without semantic discipline: the four memory rows each get a different colored dotted leader (cyan, magenta, yellow, green) for identical metric types; box titles alternate red/green/blue/magenta letters ("cpu", "mem", "net", "proc", "filter", "pause") purely as hotkey markers, so color carries no data meaning. Multiple low-contrast failures at this cell size: the GPU1 bar is dark grey on black and nearly invisible, the CPU total meter is a mid-grey block, the dotted per-core micro-bars are dim grey dots, and wattage figures ("25.2W", "11.8W", "0.00W") plus "41°C" are set in dark blue on black. The "total ▲▼ gpu-totals" title collides with the frame line; the braille graph in the net panel switches magenta/blue with no key. Numbers themselves are crisp white and right-aligned, and process rows for root are correctly dimmed, but the proc table shows no selection highlight ("0/532") and every panel border competes at equal weight, producing a flat hierarchy where nothing leads the eye.
submitted_verdict.evidence_B: Dark navy ground with a restrained palette: one accent hue per category (teal Caches, slate-blue Games, amber Downloads, green Projects, lavender Photos, red Documents) reused consistently in treemap fills, panel borders, and the proportional bars under the "LARGEST FIRST" rows, so color encodes identity. Selection is unambiguous: the Caches pane has a bright mint border and the matching list row gets a filled highlight and brighter numerals. Numeric hierarchy is layered: sizes in teal, percentages in muted grey, a hero "4.2 GiB" in the header, and dim ranks "01"–"06". Weaknesses: labels truncate at "archlinux-ol…", "video-exp…", "design-as…", "220.0 …" in panes with visible slack; two panes are unlabeled (narrow block right of "Package cache", sliver at far right of the Photos row); the hero numeral is disproportionately large for a monospace grid; and tertiary grey text ("18 files · 22 folders", "Space Add the selected item", key hints) sits at low contrast on navy. The letterspaced "D I S K  A L L O C A T I O N" title is decorative rather than functional.
submitted_verdict.loser_reason: A's palette is undisciplined: near a dozen hues are applied non-semantically (identical metrics in different colors, rainbow hotkey letters, competing colored frames) while its genuinely quantitative elements (GPU1 bar, per-core micro-bars, blue wattage and temperature figures) fall to near-invisible contrast on black, so hierarchy is flat and the eye has no reliable path through dense data.

Multiple low-contrast failures at this cell size: the GPU1 bar is dark grey on black and nearly invisible, the CPU total meter is a mid-grey block, the dotted per-core micro-bars are dim grey dots, and wattage figures ("25.2W", "11.8W", "0.00W") plus "41°C" are set in dark blue on black. The "total ▲▼ gpu-totals" title collides with the frame line; the braille graph in the net panel switches magenta/blue with no key. Numbers themselves are crisp white and right-aligned, and process rows for root are correctly dimmed, but the proc table shows no selection highlight ("0/532") and every panel border competes at equal weight, producing a flat hierarchy where nothing leads the eye.

B: Dark navy ground with a restrained palette: one accent hue per category (teal Caches, slate-blue Games, amber Downloads, green Projects, lavender Photos, red Documents) reused consistently in treemap fills, panel borders, and the proportional bars under the "LARGEST FIRST" rows, so color encodes identity.
